dataset.description:
EOSC Metadata Schema and Crosswalk Registry (MSCR)
Support publishing, discovery and access of metadata schemas and provide functions to operationalise metadata conversions by combining crosswalks.

This dataset contains two parts:

A. The metadata schema and crosswalks this MSCR service will host, will be stored as a triplet database, which will be available for access or download via an API provided by the MSCR service. This data set is open and contains no personal or copyrighted information. The metadata schema and crosswalks will be initially be provided from other such registries and upload and modification activity from authenticated users. Users will be shown a notice not to upload copyrighted material. A editorial board appointed by the project coordinator and later responsible service provider organisation can take decisions on data curation.

B. For operation of the MSCR there is need for the registration of users that want to upload and/or modify metadata schema and crosswalks in the MSCR. Registration of a minimal amount of personal information (e.g. email) may be needed, in combination of arranging for access authentication via the EOSC AAI. Special users accounts may be necessary for administrators and/or users without access to the EOSC AAI such as users from public administration and cultural heritage institutes that have an interest in the metadata crosswalks (management). The user information is cross indexed with the metadata schema and crosswalks from dataset A.
Storage and processing of this data set will be according the GDPR.

dataset.description:
The EOSC RAiD service will mint Persistent Identifiers (PIDs) for research projects. The newly minted RAiD which will the enable users to populate the RAiD metadata envelope with project information and associated PIDs for project participants, inputs and outputs. 

Use of the EOSC RAiD service will typically begin in the EOSC catalog, when a user is selecting an EOSC service. The user is prompted to register a RAiD (project identifier), whereby a unique handle identifier is assigned. The project title and short description, and identity of the user (e.g. ORCID) is stored in metadata of the newly minted RAiD. The metadata collected by the EOSC RAiD registry will be accessible by the RAiD API and resolvable in up to three configurations:

  1. open: the project identifier (handle) with project title/description and the project information will be open by default.
  2. embargoed: the project identifier (handle) with project title will be open, but everything else will be closed while under embargo. 
  3. closed: discussions are ongoing about use cases that could warrant a closed RAiD.
For this project, data will collected from the following WP7 case studies:
  1. Climate Change' / ENES case study
  2. European Integration of National-level Services Case Study
Collected data will be stored and analysed for project purposes. Storage and processing of this dataset will be in accordance with GDPR. This data will be stored during and throughout the full FAIRCORE4EOSC project timeline (through month 36). As this data is collected for service testing and validation, at project closure RAiD case study data will be safely and securely deleted and/or archived if necessary.

dataset.description:
The dataset described here covers the scope of the requirements gathering project for WP4 of FAIRCORE4EOSC. WP4 is developing three new EOSC-Core Components: 1) The Metadata Schema and Cross-walk Registry, 2) The Data Type Registry and 3) The Research Activity Identifier Registry. To this end, the requirements gathering project processes information pertaining to the requirements and specifications documented for the development of these new core components. The suppliers of this information are the teams developing these new core components, as well as the case study and demonstrator teams who represent potential users of the components.

Information that will be processed during the lifetime of the project will include:
  1. Descriptions about core component functionalities, system environments and architectures
  2. Descriptions of user stories and user experiences when interacting with these core components
  3. Collaborators' contact and organizational information
  4. Material regarding use of collaboration tools such as Jira and Confluence
All information collected during the requirements gathering project is open by default. The requirements and specifications documented for the development of the new core components is intended to be open. The contact and organizational information from collaborators is public information, such as their email address from their affiliated institute or organization. This contact information is processed while collaborators plan and work on the project on team collaboration platforms, including but not limited to, the project Confluence pages and the Jira instances for requirements descriptions and planning.

The processing of this project information began during month 1 of the project, and will endure the FAIRCORE4EOSC project timeline until month 36. A project closure and archive plan will be designed so that all information processed as part of the requirements gathering project will be safely and securely deleted if possible, and/or archived if necessary.

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan describes the management of data and some source code that will be produced in the context of the EC Horizon Europe project: Core Components Supporting a FAIR EOSC (FAIRCORE4EOSC) (Grant agreement ID: 101057264). 

The objective of the project:
FAIRCORE4EOSC focuses on the development and realisation of EOSC-Core components supporting a FAIR EOSC, addressing gaps identified in the SRIA. Leveraging existing technologies and services, the project will develop nine new EOSC-Core components aimed to improve the discoverability and interoperability of an increased amount of research outputs. FAIRCORE4EOSC will also contribute to the EOSC Interoperability Framework by establishing new guidelines on the new EOSC-Core components. The new components will be crucial to support the FAIR research life cycle. Five user-centric case studies (climate change, social sciences and humanities, mathematics, national research information systems, research data management communities) will drive the development and testing of the new components ensuring they are tailored to the user needs (co-design). All the selected case studies share similar challenges that are common to many other stakeholder groups: research communities at European and national level have datasets that currently cannot be found in the EOSC; they use Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) but they are lacking PIDs for different levels of aggregation; they use community specific services to manage metadata that make cross-discipline reuse and interoperability complex. The user stories and best practices drawn by the case studies will be used to foster uptake of the new components beyond the project partners.

The project uses some pre-existing datasets as it builds on existing solutions, but also produces some new ones or extends existing ones. Some of the datasets pertain to the EOSC core components being developed, while others relate to the communities that demonstrate the use of those components in their domain. This version of the data management plan is made before the bulk of the work of the project is carried out, and thus describes many things that are uncertain at this moment. The Data Management Plan is intended to evolve as the work progresses.
